idiom_name: immutable MonsterType class instance + IReadOnlyDictionary registry
implementation_notes: The CLR's own System.Type describes compiler types and cannot carry domain fields, so the pattern collapses into two ordinary declarations: a sealed descriptor class exposed through get-only properties, and an instance class holding a reference to it. A registry (Dictionary built once, exposed as IReadOnlyDictionary) is the single source of truth and is deserialised from JSON at startup; identity is an id, never the descriptor's value equality. Constructor-injected descriptors keep the instance valid from the first line, and a factory method on the descriptor keeps construction in one place. Use the class form when descriptors need a default constructor for a serialiser or when they must be mutated during authoring; the record form (see variants) is the modern data-carrier alternative.
pitfalls: Public setters on the descriptor let one edit retune every live monster at once; expose get-only (or init-only) properties and replace the registry entry instead.
Naming the member 'Type' shadows System.Type in reflection-heavy code and confuses serialisers - prefer 'Kind' or 'Breed'.
A Dictionary registry populated lazily from several threads can be observed half-built; build it completely, then publish it read-only (or use ConcurrentDictionary).

variants.name: Record descriptor with with-expression tuning
variants.implementation_notes: A record is a transparent, immutable carrier whose equality, ToString and copy construction are compiler-generated - the paper's 'type object as data' with the least ceremony: one record declaration per type shape, tuning expressed as 'troll with { BaseHealth = 52 }' which produces a new descriptor instead of mutating a shared one. Nondestructive mutation is exactly the pattern's tuning story (edit the type without recompiling), and the copy constructor can be customised when a member is a reference type that must be deep-copied. Registry and factory work the same as in the class variant. Prefer this form when descriptors are loaded once and never edited; records make the immutability that the pattern requires the default rather than a discipline.
pitfalls: Record value equality makes two equal-looking descriptors equal even when they are meant to be different types - key the registry by Id and compare ids, never descriptors.

The generated copy constructor (and 'with') is shallow: a mutable collection member (abilities, loot table) is shared between the original and the derived descriptor, so tuning a variant can mutate its base.
Positional records without validation let a data file construct a descriptor with a negative health; validate in the primary constructor body or use 'required' members.
